executive_summary: Following the expiration of the Orvan corridor agreement on 10 September 2026, grain imports from Orvan to Midgard and Tolan experienced substantial declines. Midgard's wheat import value loss from Orvan post-expiration ranges between USD 156.5M and USD 216.2M. Midgard's maize import loss was temporarily buffered in October by delayed delivery terms but contracted sharply in late Q4, resulting in a loss of USD 105.7M to USD 126.4M. Tolan's wheat import loss ranges from USD 69.6M to USD 96.0M. Tolan's maize exposure cannot be quantified due to missing trade data. While alternative supply via rail and Vanir shipments increased, official reports confirm these volumes are small compared to Orvan's sea trade and cannot close the supply deficit.

outlook.text: In Q1 2027, import deficits across wheat and maize routes from Orvan are expected to persist at elevated levels in the absence of a renewed maritime agreement. Importers in Midgard and Tolan will continue relying on higher-cost rail routes through Ravik and short-term contracts with Vanir. However, capacity constraints and elevated handling costs will maintain upward pressure on grain prices and limit full volume recovery.
assumptions: No replacement Orvan corridor agreement will be negotiated during Q1 2027.
Rail transport capacity through Ravik remains near current operational ceilings.
Vanir exportable grain surplus remains insufficient to offset lost Orvan maritime volumes.
